'''Marquis Devante Teague''' (born February 28, 1993) is an American former professional [[basketball]] player. He was one of the top-rated high school basketball players in the class of 2011.

==High school career==
In July 2010, Teague, along with future [[Kentucky Wildcats men's basketball|Kentucky]] teammate [[Michael Kidd-Gilchrist]], were a part of the gold medal-winning team in the [[2010 FIBA Under-17 World Championship|FIBA U-17 World Championships]] in [[Hamburg, Germany]].<ref>{{cite web|first=Corey|last=Taylor|url=https://bleacherreport.com/articles/420127-kentucky-commits-michael-gilchrist-and-marquis-teague-win-gold|title=Future Kentucky Wildcats Michael Gilchrist and Marquis Teague Win Gold|work=BleacherReport.com|date=July 14, 2010|access-date=August 26, 2010}}</ref>

Considered a five-star recruit by [[Rivals.com]], Teague was listed as the No. 1 point guard and the No. 5 player in the nation in 2011. He was a part of the Indiana versus Kentucky All-stars game.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://n.rivals.com/content/prospects/maple/77385|title=Marquis Teague Recruiting Profile|work=Rivals.com|access-date=August 26, 2010}}</ref>

==College career==
Teague committed to [[Kentucky Wildcats men's basketball|Kentucky]] on April 22, 2010.

In the first game of the [[2011–12 Kentucky Wildcats men's basketball team|2011–12 season]] and his career as a Wildcat, Teague started and scored 16 points on 7-of-12 shooting. One of Teague's best performances of the season came against [[Portland Pilots men's basketball|Portland]], a game where he scored 14 points, had a career high of eight assists, and a career high of 4 steals, all while committing no turnovers and shooting 5 of 6 from the free throw line. Against [[Louisville Cardinals men's basketball|Louisville]], Teague scored just 4 points on 1 of 8 shooting, but did dish out 5 assists and played good defense on Louisville point guard [[Peyton Siva]], who shot 2 of 13 from the field. Teague helped Kentucky win their [[2012 NCAA Division I men's basketball championship game|eighth national championship]].

==Professional career==
In April 2012, Teague declared for the [[2012 NBA draft]].<ref>{{cite web |last=Associated Press |date=April 18, 2012 |title=UK's starting five opts for draft |url=https://www.espn.com/nba/draft2012/story/_/id/7825727 |access-date=May 24, 2023 |work=ESPN |publisher=ESPN Internet Ventures}}</ref> He was selected by the [[Chicago Bulls]] with the 29th overall pick.

On December 3, 2013, Teague was assigned to the [[Iowa Energy]];<ref>{{cite web |date=December 3, 2013 |title=Bulls Assign Teague to Iowa Energy |url=https://www.nba.com/bulls/news/bulls-assign-teague-iowa-energy.html |access-date=May 24, 2023 |work=NBA.com |publisher=Turner Sports Interactive, Inc.}}</ref> he was recalled the next day.<ref>{{cite web|title=Bulls Recall Teague from D-League|url=http://www.nba.com/bulls/news/bulls-recall-teague-d-league.html|work=NBA.com|publisher=Turner Sports Interactive, Inc.|access-date=December 4, 2013|date=December 4, 2013}}</ref> On December 26, 2013, he was reassigned to the Energy.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.insidehoops.com/blog/?p=14977|title=Chicago Bulls assign Marquis Teague|work=InsideHoops.com|date=December 26, 2013|access-date=December 26, 2013}}</ref> On January 15, 2014, he was recalled.<ref>{{cite web |date=January 15, 2014 |title=Bulls Recall Guard Marquis Teague |url=https://www.nba.com/bulls/news/bulls-recall-guard-marquis-teague.html |access-date=May 24, 2023 |work=NBA.com |publisher=Turner Sports Interactive, Inc.}}</ref>

On January 21, 2014, Teague was traded to the [[Brooklyn Nets]] in exchange for [[Tornike Shengelia]].<ref>{{cite web |last=Sapp |first=Demetris |date=January 21, 2014 |title=Nets Acquire Marquis Teague From Chicago |url=https://www.nba.com/nets/news/nets-acquire-marquis-teague-chicago |access-date=May 24, 2023 |work=NBA.com |publisher=Turner Sports Interactive, Inc.}}</ref>

On October 24, 2014, Teague was traded, along with a [[2019 NBA draft|2019 second-round]] pick, to the [[Philadelphia 76ers]] in exchange for [[Casper Ware]].<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.nba.com/sixers/news/141024-trade|title=Sixers Acquire Marquis Teague And Future Second-round Draft Pick|work=NBA.com|publisher=Turner Sports Interactive, Inc.|access-date=November 19, 2014|date=October 24, 2014}}</ref> Three days later, he was waived by the 76ers.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.nba.com/sixers/news/141027-roster|title=Sixers Announce 2014-15 Opening Night Roster|work=NBA.com|publisher=Turner Sports Interactive, Inc.|access-date=November 19, 2014|date=October 27, 2014}}</ref> On November 1, 2014, he was selected by the [[Oklahoma City Blue]] with the ninth overall pick in the 2014 [[NBA Development League]] draft.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.nba.com/dleague/oklahomacity/oklahoma_city_blue_selects_six_141101.html|title=Oklahoma City Blue Selects Six in NBA D-League Draft|work=NBA.com|publisher=Turner Sports Interactive, Inc.|access-date=November 19, 2014|date=November 1, 2014|url-status=dead|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20141106214900/http://www.nba.com/dleague/oklahomacity/oklahoma_city_blue_selects_six_141101.html|archive-date=November 6, 2014}}</ref>

On November 3, 2015, Teague was reacquired by the Blue.<ref>{{cite news|title=Oklahoma City Blue Announces Training Camp Roster|url=http://oklahomacity.dleague.nba.com/news/201516_camproster/|access-date=November 9, 2015|work=NBA.com|date=November 3, 2015|archive-date=March 4, 2016|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160304104544/http://oklahomacity.dleague.nba.com/news/201516_camproster/|url-status=dead}}</ref> Teague played for the OKC Blue of the NBDL in the 2015–16 season. He averaged 15.2 points a game, 30.8 minutes a game, 5.7 field goals made, 14.2 for the field goals attempted, .726 free throw percentage, 0.9 threes a game, 2.5 threes attempted, 34% three-point accuracy, 3 free throws made, 0.4 offensive rebounds, 2.5 rebounds, 5.7 assists, 0.8 in steals a game, 0.3 blocks, 3 turnovers a game.

On July 17, 2016, Teague signed with [[Ironi Nahariya]] of the [[Israeli Basketball Premier League|Israeli League]].<ref>{{cite web|first=Igor|last=Obradovic|title=Ironi Nahariya lands Marquis Teague|url=http://www.eurobasket.com/Israel/news/454169/Ironi-Nahariya-lands-Marquis-Teague|work=Eurobasket.com|date=July 17, 2016|access-date=October 17, 2016}}</ref> On October 31, he was waived by Nahariya and on November 26, he signed in Russia with [[Avtodor Saratov]] of the [[VTB United League]].<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.sportando.com/en/cups/vtb-league/218570/avtodor-saratov-adds-marquis-teague-and-vince-hunter.html|title=Avtodor Saratov adds Marquis Teague and Vince Hunter|work=Sportando.com|date=November 26, 2016|access-date=November 26, 2016}}</ref> On March 2, 2017, Teague was acquired by the [[Fort Wayne Mad Ants]] of the NBA Development League.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://fortwayne.dleague.nba.com/news/mad-ants-finalize-trade-blue/|title=Mad Ants Finalize Trade with Blue|work=NBA.com|date=March 2, 2017|access-date=March 6, 2017}}</ref>

On August 23, 2017, Teague was selected by the [[Memphis Hustle]] in the NBA G League expansion draft.<ref>{{cite news|title=2017 NBA G League Expansion Draft Results|url=http://gleague.nba.com/news/2017-nba-g-league-expansion-draft-results/|access-date=August 23, 2017|work=NBA.com|date=August 23, 2017}}</ref>

On August 30, 2018, Teague signed with [[Jeonju KCC Egis]] of the Korean league.<ref>{{cite web |title=Marquis Teague signs with Jeonju KCC |url=https://sportando.basketball/en/asia/south-korea/287088/marquis-teague-signs-with-jeonju-kcc.html |website=Sportando |access-date=August 31, 2018}}</ref> He joined the Memphis Hustle in 2019.<ref>{{cite web |last=Langham |first=Geoff |title=Memphis Hustle announce final roster |url=https://memphis.gleague.nba.com/news/memphis-hustle-announce-final-roster-191104/ |website=NBA.com |access-date=December 5, 2019 |date=November 4, 2019 |archive-date=November 7, 2019 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20191107023529/https://memphis.gleague.nba.com/news/memphis-hustle-announce-final-roster-191104/ |url-status=dead }}</ref> Teague averaged 13.2 points and 4.3 assists per game in 2019–20 season.<ref>{{cite news |last=Varney |first=Dennis |title=Catch up with 36 ex-Cats playing pro basketball in leagues outside the NBA |url=https://www.kentucky.com/sports/college/kentucky-sports/ex-cats/article241420196.html |access-date=May 16, 2020 |work=[[Lexington Herald-Leader]] |date=March 26, 2020}}</ref>

Teague spent the 2021–22 season with the British club [[London Lions (basketball)|London Lions]], averaging 14.7 points, 2.4 rebounds, 4.6 assists and 1.2 steals in 13 games.

On September 28, 2022, Teague signed with Greek club [[Kolossos Rodou B.C.|Kolossos Rodou]]. In 19 league games, he averaged 4.3 points, 1.3 rebounds and 1.7 assists, playing around 16 minutes per contest.

==Personal life==
Teague is the son of Shawn and Carol Teague. He has four siblings, including  [[NBA All-Star]] [[Jeff Teague (basketball)|Jeff Teague]].<ref>{{cite web |last=Tipton |first=Jerry |url=http://www.kentucky.com/2010/04/23/1235430/2011-point-guard-teague-picks.html |title=Teague says 'dynasty' possible at UK | KentuckySports.com |publisher=Kentucky.com |access-date=August 26, 2010 |archive-date=August 29, 2012 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20120829085418/http://www.kentucky.com/2010/04/23/1235430/2011-point-guard-teague-picks.html |url-status=dead }}</ref> Shawn played for [[Norm Stewart]] at the [[Missouri Tigers men's basketball|University of Missouri]] before transferring to [[Boston University Terriers men's basketball statistical leaders|Boston University]], where he finished his career playing for [[Rick Pitino]];<ref>{{cite web|first=Lee|last=Jenkins|url=https://www.si.com/more-sports/2012/02/17/jeff-marquisteague|title=Teague family at heart of hoops' little-man revolution|work=SI.com|date=February 17, 2012|access-date=February 17, 2012}}</ref> he, like his brother, was an ''Indiana All-Star'' following his senior season of high school basketball.
